{{Short description|Mathematical mentod}}
In [[numerical analysis]] '''Chebyshev–Gauss quadrature''' is an extension of [[Gaussian quadrature]] method for approximating the value of integrals of the following kind:

:<math>\int_{-1}^{+1} \frac {f(x)} {\sqrt{1 - x^2} }\,dx</math>

and

:<math>\int_{-1}^{+1} \sqrt{1 - x^2} g(x)\,dx.</math>

In the first case

:<math>\int_{-1}^{+1} \frac {f(x)} {\sqrt{1-x^2} }\,dx \approx \sum_{i=1}^n w_i f(x_i)</math>

where

:<math>x_i = \cos \left( \frac {2i-1} {2n} \pi \right)</math>

and the weight

:<math>w_i = \frac {\pi} {n}.</math><ref name="AS1">Abramowitz, M & Stegun, I A, ''Handbook of Mathematical Functions'', 10th printing with corrections (1972), Dover, {{ISBN|978-0-486-61272-0}}. Equation 25.4.38.</ref>

In the second case

:<math>\int_{-1}^{+1} \sqrt{1-x^2} g(x)\,dx \approx \sum_{i=1}^n w_i g(x_i)</math>

where

:<math>x_i = \cos \left( \frac {i} {n+1} \pi \right) </math>

and the weight

:<math> w_i = \frac {\pi} {n+1} \sin^2 \left( \frac {i} {n+1} \pi \right). \,</math><ref name="AS2">Abramowitz, M & Stegun, I A, ''Handbook of Mathematical Functions'', 10th printing with corrections (1972), Dover, {{ISBN|978-0-486-61272-0}}. Equation 25.4.40.</ref>
